steps.body: A clock has two hands with two different jobs. The **SHORT hand names the hour** — a slow walker, passing one number per hour. The **LONG hand counts minutes** — a fast walker, lapping the whole face every hour. Read short first, long second.
Match each part to its job.

widget.prompt: Connect each clock part to the job it does.

right.label: Mark the hours AND the five-minute steps

pairErrors.feedback: Swapped hands — the classic clock trap! The SHORT, slow hand names the hour; minute-counting is the long hand's job.

widget.missFeedback: Short and slow names the hour; long and fast counts minutes; the numbers work double shifts.
widget.successFeedback: Short hand → hour, long hand → minutes, and the numbers moonlight as five-minute marks.

explanationVariants: Short hand at 7 names the hour; long hand straight up at 12 means zero minutes — 7:00 sharp.
Read in order: short first (7), long second (:00). The 12 is the minute hand's starting gate.

widget.successFeedback: Hour 7, zero minutes — the long hand at 12 means the hour is brand new.
widget.hourFeedback: Hands swapped! That reading treats the LONG hand as the hour (12) and the short one as minutes (7-mark = 35). Short names the hour: it's 7.
widget.minuteFeedback: The long hand pointing at 12 doesn't mean 12 minutes — the 12 is minute ZERO, the top of the lap. 7:00 exactly.

cml.actionGoal: Coordinate hour and minute positions while composing elapsed time on a 60-minute cycle.

steps.body: The minute hand has a secret code: the numbers 1–12 work **double shifts**. For the minute hand, each number is worth FIVE minutes — pointing at 3 means 15, at 6 means 30, at 9 means 45. Count by fives around the face.

explanationVariants: The 8-mark carries eight fives: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes past the hour.

widget.prompt: The MINUTE hand points at the number 8. How many minutes past the hour is it?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 reads the mark as ones — but minute marks count by FIVES. Eight fives is 40.
45 belongs to the 9-mark, one number over. The 8-mark carries 8 × 5 = 40.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Multiply the mark by 5 — that's the minute hand's code.

widget.prompt: Slide the minute hand from the 12 around to the 6, counting fives as you pass each number.
widget.lowFeedback: Keep walking — count five more minutes at every number you pass.
widget.highFeedback: Past the 6 — back up. The 6-mark is the halfway point of the lap.
widget.successFeedback: The 6-mark is 6 fives = 30 minutes: half past. A full lap (back to 12) would be 12 fives — the whole hour.

predict.prompt: You'll walk the minute hand around to the 6. When it points at the 6, how many minutes have passed?
predict.reveal: Each number the hand passes is worth FIVE minutes, not one — reaching the 6 takes six fives of minutes, far more than six.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents read clock.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for read clock must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines read clock.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: The hour hand travels WITH the minutes — at half past, it has drifted halfway to the next number.
That drift is a feature: on a clock with no minute hand at all, the short hand's position still tells you roughly how far into the hour you are.

widget.prompt: At 7:30, where is the HOUR hand?

options.label: Halfway between the 7 and the 8
options.feedback: Half the hour gone, half the walk done — the short hand drifts as the minutes pass.

options.label: Exactly on the 7
options.feedback: It sits ON the 7 only at 7:00 sharp. By half past, it has crept halfway toward 8 — it never waits.

options.label: On the 6
options.feedback: The 6 is where the MINUTE hand points at :30. The hour hand lives between its two numbers: 7 and 8.

options.label: Exactly on the 8
options.feedback: It reaches the 8 only when 8:00 arrives — at 7:30 it's mid-journey, halfway there.

hints: Which hand is SHORT? That one names the hour.
Short hand a bit past 2 → the hour is 2. Long hand on the 4 → apply the fives code.
The wrong reading treated the long hand as the hour.
explanationVariants: Short hand past 2 makes the hour 2; long hand at the 4-mark is 4 × 5 = 20 minutes: 2:20. The 4:10 reading swapped the hands — the long hand became 'hour 4' and the short hand near 2 became 'the 2-mark, 10 minutes.'
Swap-check: a real 4:10 would need the SHORT hand near 4 and the long hand at the 2-mark — the opposite of this clock.

widget.prompt: A clock shows: SHORT hand a bit past the 2, LONG hand on the 4. Dee reads it as 4:10. What time is it really — and what went wrong?

options.label: 2:20 — Dee swapped the hands (and read the 2-mark as ten minutes)
options.feedback: Hour from the short hand (2), minutes from the long one (4-mark = 20). Dee ran the whole read backwards.

options.label: 4:10 — Dee is right
options.feedback: Check which hand is which: the SHORT hand names the hour, and it's near 2, not 4. The long hand at the 4-mark counts 20 minutes.
Right hour, wrong code — the long hand's 4-mark counts by fives: 20 minutes, not 4.
Hands swapped AND the fives code skipped — short-near-2 names hour 2, and the 4-mark carries 20 minutes: 2:20.

steps.body: You can read any clock face now.
takeaways: Short hand names the hour; long hand counts the minutes — read short first.
Minute marks count by fives: the 8-mark is 40, never 8.
The hour hand drifts with the minutes — halfway through the hour, halfway to the next number.
steps.teaser: next: saying times sideways — 'ten to eight' and 'quarter past.'

concept.body: Quick rewind. Memory hook: **the SHORT hand has the SHORT job** — point at one number and name the hour. The LONG hand runs the LONG lap, counting all sixty minutes. Short first, long second, every read.

explanationVariants: Short at 3 names hour 3; long at 12 means zero minutes: 3:00.
The 12 is the minute hand's starting gate — a fresh hour.

widget.prompt: SHORT hand on the 3, LONG hand on the 12. The time is…

options.feedback: Hour 3, minutes zero — clean and simple.
Swapped — the short hand names the hour, and it points at 3. The long hand at 12 means the hour just began.
The long hand at 12 is minute ZERO — the top of the lap, not twelve minutes.
